result.topic_en: Euler notes that any residue can be represented by any member of its class mP+ε, including negative numbers, so that all residues can be expressed by numbers not exceeding half the prime divisor; he then observes that the powers of a root may or may not produce all residues below P, with examples a=1, a=P−1 and P=7, a=3.
result.transcription:
PER NVMERVS PRIMOS. 87
8. Cum cuiusque ordinis natura residuo ipsi proprio determinetur, quilibet cuiusque ordinis numerus eius naturam perinde declarat, ac primus, qui ipsum residuum exhibet. Hinc nihil impedit, quominus idem residuum $\varepsilon$ per quemlibet alium numerum eiusdem ordinis $mP+\varepsilon$ denotetur.
9. Ita idem residuum $\varepsilon$ non solum per numeros positiuos $\varepsilon+P$, $\varepsilon+2P$ etc. indicare licebit, sed etiam per negatiuos $\varepsilon-P$, $\varepsilon-2P$ etc. Cum igitur, si $\varepsilon$ sit diuisoris $P$ semisse maius, $\varepsilon-P$ eodem sit minus, patet numeros negatiuos admittendo, omnia residua numeris, qui diuisoris $P$ semissem non superent, exprimi posse.
Obseruationes.
10. Proposito diuisore primo $P$, prout progressionis geometricae radix $a$ constituatur, fieri potest, vt in residuis vel omnes numeri ipso $P$ minores occurrant, vel non omnes. Si enim sumatur radix $a=1$, omnia residua in vnitatem abeunt, ac si sumatur $a=P-1$, series residuorum prodit:
$1,\ P-1,\ 1,\ P-1,\ 1,\ P-1$ etc.
vel $+1,\ -1,\ +1,\ -1,\ +1,\ -1$ etc. (9).
11. Quod autem interdum omnes numeri diuisore $P$ minores in residuis occurrunt, vnico exemplo declarasse sufficiat; sit scilicet $P=7$ et sumatur radix $a=3$, habebitur:
progr. geom. $1,\ 3,\ 3^2,\ 3^3,\ 3^4,\ 3^5,\ 3^6,\ 3^7,\ 3^8,\ 3^9$ etc.
Residua $1,\ 3,\ 2,\ 6,\ 4,\ 5,\ 1,\ 3,\ 2,\ 6$ etc.
12. Si

items.quote: patet numeros negatiuos admittendo, omnia residua numeris, qui diuisoris $P$ semissem non superent, exprimi posse.
items.english: it is clear that, by admitting negative numbers, all residues can be expressed by numbers not exceeding half of the divisor P.

items.quote: Proposito diuisore primo $P$, prout progressionis geometricae radix $a$ constituatur, fieri potest, vt in residuis vel omnes numeri ipso $P$ minores occurrant, vel non omnes.
items.english: Given a prime divisor P, depending on how the root a of the geometric progression is chosen, it can happen that either all numbers less than P occur among the residues, or not all.
